terms.grammar: petere with the accusative: the bare name of a town, or another place noun
terms.comment: A plain question of ours: petere is to make for, travel to a place (Lewis & Short: Cyzicum, Cic. Fam. 14.4.3). Traupman asks whether a bus or train stops at a place with Subsistitne … in …? (218). No reference work we searched has a question for “is this the train to …?”.

phrases.latin: Petitne haec autoraeda longa forum? — Petit; īnscende.
phrases.english: Is this the bus to the town centre? — It is; get on.

sources: Lewis & Short: peto
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 218.
